title: A shop's Net term reaches QuickBooks as a standard term on first use
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The test organization is connected to a QuickBooks Online sandbox company, and you can sign in to that company in another tab.
  • The shop's own term {Term-A}, due 14 days after the invoice date, is not in QuickBooks' Terms list. Customer {Customer-A} holds {Term-A} and work order {Work-order-1} for it is complete.
    For example: {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S8-01 Fourteen, {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S8-01 Customer and {Work-order-1} is S2-15440.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. On {Work-order-1}'s Finance tab, set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  2. Click Create Invoice.
  3. Wait until the invoice has synced to QuickBooks (it is no longer on the QB Unexported report).
  4. In QuickBooks, open the Terms list (Settings, All lists, Terms).
  5. In QuickBooks, open the invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the Due date reads Oct 19, 2026.
  • Step 2: the invoice is created.
  • Step 3: the invoice is no longer on the QB Unexported report.
  • Step 4: a term named exactly {Term-A} now exists, set as a standard term due in 14 days.
  • Step 5: its terms read {Term-A} and its due date is Oct 19, 2026, the same as in ShopView.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11677 (Story 8, QuickBooks sync - credit terms)

  • S8-R1: “When a record is sent to QuickBooks with a term QuickBooks does not have, ShopView first creates the term in QuickBooks under the same name, then sends the record. This is how the standard terms already work today.”
  • S8-R2: “A "Due Net X days" term is created in QuickBooks as a standard term due in X days.”
  • S8-R5: “Each invoice carries its own term and due date to QuickBooks, as today. A vendor invoice is sent to QuickBooks as a bill with its stored due date (S7-R9) and the vendor's term at the moment it is sent.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
